HOUSEHOLD AND PERSONAL EFFECTS INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
Policy wording "WD-2026" - Robbery and Personal Effects Edition

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated
in the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

This insurance protects the policyholder against the financial consequences of
the loss of, or physical damage to, insured movable property. The perils that
can be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - among them
the taking of property by force or under threat of force, burglary, fire,
escape of water and the natural hazards. Which of the insurable perils are
actually covered is agreed between insurer and policyholder and recorded in the
schedule.

Where insured property is taken, destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies
the value of that property, or the cost of putting it back, on the basis set out
in Part 6 and within the sums insured and sub-limits agreed. A limited range of
consequential expenses triggered by a loss event is also carried, within the
limits agreed for each head.

This contract indemnifies the loss of, and physical damage to, insured property
only. It does not indemnify the expense of pursuing, evidencing, translating,
documenting or administering a claim, and it is not a legal-expenses, liability,
service or assistance contract.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage or an item of property for which no cover
exists. Exclusions delimit what has been promised and keep the cover calculable.
They appear as general exclusions applying across the contract, within the
provisions on individual perils, and within the description of the insured
property.

Affected item - an item of insured property which was taken, destroyed, damaged
or lost in the insured event, and which is identified as such in the itemisation
under 7.1.10.

Indemnifiable loss - the value of the affected items, determined under Part 6
and Part 7, before the application of sub-limits and of the deductible.

Sub-limit - a monetary ceiling that applies within the sum insured to a defined
class of property or to a defined head of cost. Where a sub-limit applies, the
class or head is indemnified only up to that ceiling; the excess is borne by the
policyholder. Where the loss on that class or head remains below the ceiling,
the sub-limit does not reduce the indemnity.

Ancillary charge - any charge raised alongside the value of the affected items
themselves: carriage, freight, delivery, dispatch, packaging, postage,
transport, call-out and travel, translation, transcription, notarisation,
certification, reporting, administration, handling and comparable items.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before,
during and after an insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is taken, destroyed or damaged by,
or lost as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) TAKING BY FORCE - the taking of insured property from the policyholder,
      or from a person living with the policyholder in the same household, by
      the use of force against that person or under the threat of an immediate
      danger to life or limb;

  (b) BURGLARY AND COMPARABLE INTERFERENCE with the insured premises or with a
      locked receptacle;

  (c) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot;

  (d) ESCAPE OF WATER;

  (e) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (e1) storm and hail;
        (e2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the groups (a), (b), (c), (d) and (e1) can be taken separately. The
further natural hazards under (e2) can only be taken in combination with one or
more of the other groups.

2.3 The taking by force defined

2.3.1 Force and threat
Force means the physical overcoming of a resistance offered, or reasonably to be
expected, by the person from whom the property is taken. A threat suffices where
it is directed at an immediate danger to life or limb and where the property is
surrendered on account of it.

2.3.2 Property taken outside the insured premises
Cover extends to insured property carried on the person, or carried in immediate
personal custody, away from the insured premises, insofar as this is agreed in
the schedule and within the sub-limits stated there.

2.3.3 Reporting requirement
The event must be reported without delay to the competent public authority and
the reference of that report given with the claim. The report is a condition of
cover; the cost of obtaining, translating or otherwise processing it is governed
by 3.1.6 and 7.1.8.

2.3.4 Damage excluded within this group
Not covered:
  (a) property mislaid, misplaced, forgotten, left behind or lost without an
      event within the meaning of 2.3.1;
  (b) property surrendered voluntarily, including on a deception, a false
      pretext or an inducement not involving force or threat within the meaning
      of 2.3.1;
  (c) a shortfall established only on a subsequent stocktaking or reconciliation
      and not attributable to an identified event.

2.4 Burglary defined

Burglary is present where the perpetrator breaks into, forces open or enters by
comparable means the insured premises or a locked receptacle within them, or
uses a key or code obtained through an insured event under 2.3.

2.5 Fire group, escape of water and natural hazards

2.5.1 The fire group covers fire - a combustion that has started without a
hearth intended for it, or that has escaped such a hearth, and that is capable
of spreading under its own power - together with lightning strike, overvoltage
caused by lightning, explosion, deflagration, implosion, aircraft impact,
vehicle impact, scorching, and smoke and soot. Damage from the gradual action of
smoke or soot is not covered.

2.5.2 Escaping water means water that has emerged contrary to its intended
purpose from the water, heating, air-conditioning, extinguishing or comparable
installations of the building in which the insured property is located.

2.5.3 Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale
threshold on the recognised scale of wind strength; hail means solid
precipitation in the form of grains of ice. The further natural hazards are
flood, backing-up of water, earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load,
avalanche and volcanic eruption, each as customarily defined.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered, irrespective of any
contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.4 Liability risks
Claims of third parties against the policyholder, and any outlay directed at
covering, assessing, administering or settling such claims, are not the subject
of this contract.

3.1.5 Service, assistance and administration arrangements
Outlay arising from a service, assistance, support, handling, representation or
comparable arrangement, and any charge for placing, registering, administering
or executing an order under such an arrangement, is not indemnifiable. This
applies irrespective of whether the arrangement was entered into on the occasion
of an insured event, and irrespective of whether the charge is raised by a party
that also renders an indemnifiable benefit.

3.1.6 Preparation and substantiation of the claim
Establishing, evidencing and presenting the claim is a matter for the
policyholder at its own expense. Outlay directed at the cause, the extent or the
substantiation of the loss, or at rendering the supporting documents usable for
the purposes of the claim, is not an indemnifiable head of loss under this
contract. This applies in particular to the obtaining, copying, certifying,
notarising, transcribing, summarising, translating into or out of any language,
interpreting, formatting or filing of reports, statements, records, receipts,
valuations and comparable documents, however necessary those steps may be for
the claim to be assessed, and whoever performs them. Part 8 and the general
contract provisions govern the allocation of the costs of an expert
determination; nothing in this clause affects the policyholder's own duty of
substantiation under 7.1.10.

3.2 Exclusions relating to particular property

Not covered is loss of or damage to property which was, at the time of the
insured event, in the custody of a carrier, a repairer, a dealer or another
third party for a purpose unconnected with the insured event, save where
otherwise agreed.

3.3 Exclusions within the escape of water peril

Damage caused by splash or cleaning water; by dry rot and house-rot fungi; by
groundwater, surface water, flood, precipitation or a backing-up brought about
by these; by earthquake, snow load, avalanche or volcanic eruption; by ground
subsidence or landslip not caused by escaping water; by the perils of the fire
group; or by storm or hail, is not covered.

3.4 Exclusions within the natural hazards

Damage caused by storm surge; by the penetration of precipitation or dirt
through openings that were not properly closed; by groundwater save where it
emerged at the surface as a result of precipitation or overflow; by the perils
of the fire group, save where triggered by an insured earthquake; and by drought
or desiccation, is not covered.

3.5 Outlay that is not an indemnity for property

Outlay that does not represent the value of an affected item, or the cost of
making good physical damage to an affected item, is not indemnified. The
delimitation is governed by 7.1.5 to 7.1.10.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises the movable items belonging to the household of the
policyholder and serving its private use, insofar as the policyholder owns them
or bears the risk for them, together with the classes of property described in
4.2 within the sub-limits stated in the schedule.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 General household effects
Movable items of ordinary household use, insured up to the sum insured stated in
the schedule.

4.2.2 Valuables
Items of jewellery, timepieces, precious metals and stones, collections and
comparable items of concentrated value form a single class of property.
Indemnity for this class is subject to the valuables sub-limit stated in the
schedule, applied per item and, where more than one such item is affected, in
the aggregate per insured event across all items, all providers and all
invoices. Where a separate valuables schedule listing an individual item and its
agreed value forms part of the contract, that agreed value applies in place of
the per-item sub-limit for that item; in the absence of such a schedule the
per-item sub-limit applies whatever the actual value of the item.

4.2.3 Means of payment
Cash, cash equivalents, prepaid and stored-value instruments and comparable
means of payment form a single class of property. Indemnity for this class is
subject to the means-of-payment sub-limit stated in the schedule, applied in the
aggregate per insured event.

4.2.4 Property carried outside the insured premises
Insured property carried on the person or in immediate personal custody away
from the insured premises is covered within the sub-limit stated in the schedule
for that situation, in addition to the class sub-limits under 4.2.2 and 4.2.3,
whichever ceiling is the lower being the operative one.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) property used predominantly for a trade, business or profession;
  (b) motor vehicles, watercraft and aircraft and their parts and accessories;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs, and the restoration, migration,
      re-licensing or re-configuration of software, media content, user accounts
      and comparable intangible items;
  (d) documents, entitlements, credit balances and comparable intangible assets
      as such, and the cost of their cancellation, blocking, replacement,
      re-issue or re-registration;
  (e) property acquired on the occasion of the loss which does not replace an
      affected item of the same kind and intended purpose.

4.4 Optionally insurable

Individual items may be scheduled at an agreed value, and classes of property
may be insured at raised sub-limits, where this is agreed and recorded in the
schedule.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the dwelling stated in the schedule together with the
ancillary rooms belonging to it. Cover away from the insured location exists
only within 4.2.4.

4.6 Several persons entitled

Where several persons are entitled under this contract, the insurer may render
its benefit to any one of them with effect for all. Conduct of one entitled
person which releases the insurer from liability does not, of itself, prejudice
the entitlement of the others.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. Deductibles can be agreed individually and may
differ from one insured peril and one insured benefit to another. Each is set
out in the schedule. The deductible is applied once per insured event to the
covered settlement, irrespective of the number of items, providers or invoices
involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) the cost of averting or mitigating the loss, insofar as the measure could
      reasonably be regarded as necessary in the circumstances;
  (b) the cost of clearing away and disposing of destroyed insured property;
  (c) the cost of moving and protecting insured property;
  (d) the cost of changing locks of the insured premises where keys were taken
      in an insured event;
  (e) hotel costs where the insured premises have become uninhabitable.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it.
This list is exhaustive. A head of cost that does not fall within it is not
insured, however closely it is connected with the insured event and however
reasonably it was incurred.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Averting and mitigating the loss
Costs of measures taken during or immediately after the insured event to prevent
the loss from occurring or from increasing, capped at [amount] per insured
event. Steps taken after the loss has come to rest, and directed at the pursuit
of the claim rather than at the property, do not fall under this head (3.1.6).

5.2.2 Clearing away and disposal
Costs incurred in clearing away and disposing of the remains of destroyed
insured property, including transport to the nearest disposal site.

5.2.3 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting property, where those measures
serve to secure or reinstate insured property. This head does not extend to the
carriage, freight, delivery, dispatch or transport of newly procured property to
the insured location, nor to the transport or forwarding of documents.

5.2.4 Change of locks
Costs of replacing the locks of the insured premises where their keys were taken
in an insured event, capped at [amount] per insured event.

5.2.5 Hotel costs
Costs of accommodation where the insured premises have become uninhabitable and
confining oneself to a habitable part cannot reasonably be expected, reimbursed
only where indemnity cannot be claimed under another insurance contract, up to
[amount] per day for a maximum of [number] days.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. It is
determined separately for each class of property under 4.2.

6.2 Replacement value

6.2.1 What is insured is the amount that would have to be spent to procure
property of the same kind and quality in new condition at the time of the
insured event.

6.2.2 For items whose current value has fallen to a substantial extent below the
replacement value - in particular through age, wear, technical obsolescence or
lack of use - the current value applies in place of the replacement value.

6.2.3 For items of concentrated value within 4.2.2, the insurable value is the
amount that would have to be spent to procure an item of the same kind, quality,
grade and craftsmanship, determined at the time of the insured event and
evidenced under 7.1.10.

6.2.4 For the means of payment within 4.2.3, the insurable value is the nominal
value.

6.3 Relationship between basis of cover and sub-limits

The basis of cover under 6.2 does not displace a sub-limit. Where a class of
property carries a sub-limit, the sub-limit determines the ceiling of the
indemnity for that class even where the insurable value demonstrably exceeds it,
and the balance is borne by the policyholder. Conversely, a sub-limit is a
ceiling and not a fixed benefit: where the indemnifiable loss on that class is
lower, the indemnity is the loss.

6.4 Permanently devalued property

For property that can no longer be used for its purpose, only the achievable
sale price is insured.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the sum insured, the area and type of
the insured premises, the sub-limits agreed, the deductible agreed, other agreed
features material to the premium calculation, and the adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted, the premium changes accordingly. The adjustment factor
changes with effect from 1 January of each year in line with the movement of the
relevant published price indices, weighted as agreed and rounded to two decimal
places.

6.7 Subsequent change in a premium-rating feature

Where a rating circumstance subsequently changes and a higher premium results,
the insurer may demand the higher premium from the point at which the change is
notified. Where such a circumstance ceases to apply and a lower premium results,
the insurer must reduce the premium from the point at which it becomes aware of
that.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for taken, destroyed or lost items - the insurable value under Part 6 at
      the time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged items - the necessary repair costs at the time of the insured
      event, together with any diminution in value the repair does not offset,
      capped at the insurable value of the item;
  (c) for the means of payment - the nominal value.

Where the property concerned belongs to a class carrying a sub-limit, the
indemnity under (a), (b) or (c) is in every case confined to that sub-limit.

7.1.2 Where property that was taken is recovered, the policyholder must notify
the insurer without delay. Property recovered before the indemnity is paid is
treated as damaged property; property recovered afterwards is either surrendered
to the insurer or retained against repayment of the indemnity.

7.1.3 Price increases occurring between the insured event and the replacement
are indemnified where the replacement is secured within [number] months.

7.1.4 The achievable sale price of remains is set off in calculating the
indemnity.

7.1.5 Extent of the indemnity
Indemnity is confined to those items of insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event. Property supplied, procured, renewed or
supplemented in connection with the replacement of an affected item, without
having been itself affected, is not indemnified, whatever its functional
necessity for putting the replacement into use, and whatever its proportion of
the invoice.

7.1.6 Sets and matched items
Where one item of a set, suite, pair or collection was affected, indemnity is
confined to that item and does not extend to the remaining, unaffected items,
whatever the loss of uniformity, completeness or resale value.

7.1.7 What forms part of the indemnity for property
The indemnity under 7.1.1 comprises the value of the affected item, or the
labour and materials directed at repairing the physical damage to that item
itself. It comprises nothing further.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not an indemnity for property
The following are not indemnified, however they may be described, bundled or
invoiced, by whichever party they are raised, and irrespective of whether they
appear on an invoice or settlement statement that also contains an indemnifiable
element:

  (a) measures directed at the general condition, upkeep, security, compliance,
      modernisation or improvement of property, as distinct from making good the
      damage caused by the insured event;

  (b) carriage, freight, delivery, dispatch, packaging, postage, courier,
      transport, logistics and comparable charges, whether for bringing
      replacement property to the insured location, for forwarding documents or
      correspondence, or for returning items, and whether stated as a separate
      line, as a percentage or as a flat rate;

  (c) fitting, mounting, installing, connecting, commissioning, setting up,
      configuring or instructing in the use of replacement property;

  (d) call-out, travel, journey, mileage, vehicle, attendance and standby
      charges, save where incurred on the occasion of, and on the same invoice
      as, a benefit that is itself indemnifiable; where nothing billed on an
      invoice is indemnifiable, the attendance charge on that invoice is not
      indemnifiable either. Where indemnifiable, one such charge per invoice is
      reimbursed; return visits and repeat journeys in respect of the same
      insured event are not;

  (e) outlay belonging to a provider's own business operation rather than to the
      indemnifiable benefit - its own tools, equipment, software, licences,
      stationery, printing, copying, media, consumables and comparable working
      materials, whether described as materials, expenses, disbursements or a
      surcharge, and general administrative, handling, order-processing,
      claim-processing, file-opening or documentation charges levied in addition
      to the itemised benefit;

  (f) charges of the kind described in 3.1.4, 3.1.5 and 3.1.6, including in
      particular any charge for translating, interpreting, transcribing,
      certifying, notarising, summarising or otherwise processing a document for
      the purposes of the claim, together with any working material, surcharge or
      ancillary charge raised alongside such a charge;

  (g) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of
      the same insured event, whether by one provider or across several; only the
      first such charge is indemnified.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
The indemnity proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade, size, capacity
and specification of the affected item immediately before the insured event.
Where a higher specification, a larger format, a superior material or a premium
range is chosen instead, indemnity is limited to the cost of an equivalent
standard-grade replacement corresponding to what was in place before the loss;
the difference is borne by the policyholder.

7.1.10 Itemisation, evidence and apportionment
The policyholder itemises each affected item - its description, its approximate
age or date of acquisition, and its value - so that the sub-limits under Part 4
can be applied to each class and, where applicable, to each item. Where that
itemisation is not provided for an item, the item is not indemnified, however
plausible its inclusion in the claim may appear from the other items. Where an
invoice or settlement statement bundles indemnifiable and non-indemnifiable
elements without separate pricing, and the split cannot be established from the
documents, the line is assessed by its predominant stated purpose; where the
predominant purpose is not indemnifiable, the line is not indemnified. Where a
line bundles several affected items of a class carrying a sub-limit, the
sub-limit is applied to the line as a whole.

7.2 Devalued property

Insofar as property can no longer be used for its purpose, it is indemnified at
the achievable sale price.

7.3 Sum insured lower or higher than the insurable value

Where the sum insured is lower than the insurable value at the time of the
insured event, the indemnity is reduced in the proportion the sum insured bears
to the insurable value, insofar as this is agreed. Where the sum insured is
higher, the insurer is not obliged to compensate more than the loss actually
incurred.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they
were actually incurred, and the indemnity limits agreed for each head are
applied.

7.5 Order of application

The indemnity is determined in the following order: the indemnifiable loss is
established item by item under 7.1; the class sub-limits under Part 4 are then
applied; the insured costs under Part 5 are added within their own limits; and
the deductible under 7.8 is deducted once from the resulting amount.

7.6 Replacement element of the indemnity

Where the basis of cover is the replacement value, the policyholder acquires a
claim to that part of the indemnity which exceeds the current value only where it
demonstrates that it has secured the replacement of property of the same kind and
intended purpose within the period under 7.1.3.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred on the occasion of the replacement or repair, and not where the
policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed, once per
insured event.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim
as to its basis and its amount. One month after notifying the loss, the
policyholder may claim as an interim payment the amount that is, on the
prevailing assessment, payable as a minimum.

7.10 Repayment

The policyholder must repay indemnity paid on the replacement basis where,
through its own fault, the property was not replaced within a reasonable period,
and must repay indemnity for property subsequently recovered and retained.

7.11 Interest

The indemnity bears interest from the notification of the loss, save where paid
within one month. The rate is [number] percentage point(s) below the applicable
statutory base rate, but at least [percentage] and at most [percentage] per
year.

7.12 Suspension of time limits

Any period during which the indemnity cannot be determined or paid owing to the
fault of the policyholder is left out of account.

7.13 Deferral of payment

The insurer may defer payment for as long as there is doubt as to the
policyholder's entitlement to receive payment, or official or criminal
proceedings arising out of this insured event are pending.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the
amount of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer
and policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly, and may agree to
extend it to further determinations relating to the insured event.

8.2 Each party nominates one expert in text form. Where a party fails to
nominate within two weeks of a request, the requesting party may have the expert
appointed by the court with local jurisdiction for the loss location. Before
beginning their determinations, the two experts nominate a third expert as
umpire.

8.3 The experts' findings must state a schedule of the taken, destroyed, damaged
and lost insured property with the corresponding insurable values; the repair
and replacement costs; the residual values; and the insured costs. Where a class
of property carries a sub-limit, the findings state the loss for that class
separately, so that the sub-limit can be applied to it.

8.4 Each expert transmits its findings to both parties simultaneously. Where the
findings diverge, the umpire decides the points that remain in dispute within
the limits set by the experts' findings. The findings are binding unless they
manifestly deviate substantially from the true state of affairs.

8.5 Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert; the costs of the umpire are borne in equal shares. A report, valuation,
translation or other document obtained by one party outside this procedure
remains that party's own cost (3.1.6).

8.6 The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's
duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Duties before an insured event

9.1.1 The insured premises must be kept secured in the customary manner; doors
and windows must be locked when the premises are left unattended.

9.1.2 Items of concentrated value within 4.2.2 must be kept in the manner agreed
in the schedule when not in use or in immediate personal custody.

9.1.3 Where property is carried away from the insured premises, it must be kept
in immediate personal custody or in a locked receptacle appropriate to its
value.

9.2 Duties after an insured event

9.2.1 The policyholder must avert and mitigate the loss so far as can reasonably
be expected, and follow the insurer's instructions where these can be obtained.

9.2.2 The policyholder must report the event without delay to the competent
public authority where required under 2.3.3, must notify the insurer without
delay, and must keep the affected state unchanged until released.

9.2.3 The policyholder must provide the itemisation and the supporting documents
under 7.1.10 and give the insurer any information required to assess the claim.
The expense of doing so is borne by the policyholder (3.1.6).

9.3 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of these duties, and subject to the
conditions set out in the general contract provisions, the insurer is entitled to
terminate the contract and may be wholly or partly released from liability.

9.4 Increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification may exist in particular where the
insured premises are left unoccupied for a prolonged period, where the agreed
security arrangements are altered or cease to be operational, or where the
composition or the value of a class of property under 4.2 changes materially.
The consequences of an increase in risk are governed by the general contract
provisions.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION AND CHANGE OF CIRCUMSTANCES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation after an insured event

After an insured event for which the insurer has rendered a benefit, or has
declined to do so, each party may cancel the contract, observing a notice period
of one month, within one month of the conclusion of the negotiations on the
indemnity.

10.2 Change of the insured premises

Where the policyholder moves the household to other premises, cover passes to
those premises. Both sets of premises are covered during the removal, for a
maximum of [number] months. The change must be notified to the insurer without
delay in text form.

10.3 Change of the rating features

Where a rating feature changes, 6.7 applies. The insurer may cancel the contract
where the policyholder does not agree to a premium adjusted in accordance with
6.7, observing a notice period of one month.

10.4 Duties of notification

Changes of the kind described in 10.2 and 10.3 must be notified without delay in
text form. Where notification has been omitted, the insurer is not obliged to
pay in the insured event only where the event occurred later than one month
after notification ought to have been received and the insurer demonstrates that
it would not have concluded the existing contract on the changed circumstances.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 11 - LOSS DESCRIPTION AND OPERATIVE PROVISIONS FOR THIS CLAIM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

11.1 Insured property was taken from the policyholder in circumstances falling
within 2.3.1 while the policyholder was away from the insured premises. The
event was reported to the competent public authority at the time. The affected
items belong to classes of property for which sub-limits are agreed in the
schedule, and no separate valuables schedule listing an individual item and its
agreed value forms part of this contract.

11.2 The claim is supported by documents drawn up in a language other than the
language of the contract. Charges were subsequently raised by more than one
party: one for rendering those supporting documents usable for the purposes of
the claim, together with the working materials raised alongside that charge, and
one settlement statement in respect of the property itself, on which an
ancillary charge for forwarding was also raised.

11.3 The indemnity for the property itself is determined under 7.1.1 and then
confined to the applicable class sub-limits under 4.2.2 and 4.2.3 in accordance
with 6.3 and 7.5. Where the indemnifiable loss on a class exceeds its sub-limit,
the balance is borne by the policyholder; where it does not, the loss is paid in
full subject only to 7.8.

11.4 Clauses 2.3.1, 2.3.3, 3.1.5, 3.1.6, 4.2.2, 4.2.3, 4.2.4, 6.3, 7.1.1, 7.1.5,
7.1.7, 7.1.8(b), 7.1.8(e), 7.1.8(f), 7.1.10, 7.5 and 7.8 are the operative
provisions for determining how each line of each invoice and settlement
statement in this claim is characterised.
